title: playwright.config.ts explained
summary: The config decides where tests are, which browsers run (projects), the base URL, timeouts, retries, reporters and what to record (trace, screenshot, video).
why: Most 'it works locally but not in CI' problems are config problems. Reading the config is the fastest way to understand any Playwright repo you join.
body:
defineConfig() gives you type-checked options. Top-level options apply to the runner (testDir, timeout, retries, workers, reporter). `use` sets defaults for fixtures (baseURL, trace, screenshot, viewport). `projects` run the same tests with different `use` settings — typically one per browser or device. `webServer` can start your app before the tests.

The Prerequisites panel in this lab shows the exact config the hub generates for every run.
objectives: Find testDir, baseURL, projects, retries and reporter in a config
Know the difference between top-level options and `use`
pitfalls: Hard-coding full URLs in tests instead of baseURL.
retries > 0 locally — it hides flakiness while you develop.
